book_title: Chapter 3: How the Cash Flows Through the Pipes
question: How do Google's ad auctions, partner revenue-shares, custom TPU supply chain, and billing cycles convert $402.8B of revenue into $164.7B of operating cash flow?

epigraph.quote: Distribution is what gets you the query; unit economics is what determines how much of the click survives Traffic Acquisition Costs and silicon depreciation.
epigraph.author: Digital Infrastructure Unit-Economics Primer

web_blocks.title: Distribution Loops: Defaults, Self-Serve Auctions & Enterprise Channels

web_blocks.html: Alphabet runs three distinct go-to-market machines. First, Search & YouTube use self-serve auctions (Google Ads and DV360) for millions of SMBs and agencies with almost no sales friction [18]. Traffic arrives organically via Chrome, Android, and direct google.com visits, or via paid deals with OEMs and Apple. Under Judge Mehta's December 2025 Search order, exclusive default contracts are banned [8]. Alphabet must now compete on non-exclusive placement and product quality [8].

Second, Google Cloud runs a direct enterprise salesforce alongside global systems-integrator (SI) partners [15]. Multi-year committed-spend contracts keep working-capital drag low and revenue visibility high. Its $561 billion Q3 2026 backlog proves that demand, with >55% expected to recognize over the next 24 months [6]. Third, Other Bets (Waymo) runs a vertical physical-digital supply chain [14]. It buys base electric vehicles (Jaguar I-PACE, Zeekr/Hyundai platforms), fits Waymo Driver sensor kits, and manages depot charging and maintenance [14].

web_blocks.title: Supply Chain: Custom TPU Silicon & Global Data-Center Infrastructure

web_blocks.html: Beneath Alphabet's software sits one of the largest physical supply chains on earth. Alphabet designs custom Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) in-house with Broadcom and fabricates them at TSMC [15]. It also buys Nvidia GPUs for third-party Cloud clients [15]. Owning the TPU stack shields Search, YouTube, and Gemini inference from merchant GPU gross margins. Those same Cloud TPU sales helped double Cloud revenue in Q3 2026 [5, 6]. Yet scaling this stack demands huge upfront cash for land, hyperscale shells, liquid cooling, power interconnects, and server racks. CapEx jumped from $52.5 billion in FY2024 to $91.4 billion in FY2025, then hit $131.9 billion in 9M 2026 [3, 4, 5, 11].

web_blocks.title: Unit Economics: TAC Compression, Working Capital & FY2025 Cash Waterfall

web_blocks.html: On the ad side, Traffic Acquisition Costs (TAC) hit $59,926 million in FY2025 and $16.37 billion in Q3 2026 [10, 11]. That FY2025 figure equaled 20.3% of Google ad revenue, down from 20.7% in FY2024 [10, 11]. The falling TAC rate reflects faster growth in owned Search and YouTube versus lower-margin Google Network, where publishers keep ~68% [10]. Working capital stays structurally tight. Ad buyers pay by card or 30-day invoice, keeping Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) low while payables and accrued revenue shares help fund daily operations.

web_blocks.caption: FY2025 Audited Cash & Earnings Waterfall (USD Millions, Form 10-K). Note: 'employee_cost' maps to R&D ($61,087M, primarily engineering talent); 'other_opex' maps to Sales & Marketing ($28,693M) + General & Administrative ($21,482M); 'other_income' ($30,523M) minus 'interest' ($736M) equals net Other Income & Expense of $29,787M.
web_blocks.takeaway: In FY2025, Alphabet converted $402,836M of revenue into $129,039M of operating income (32.0% margin) and $164,713M of operating cash flow (40.9% CFO margin), before $91,447M of CapEx left $73,266M of free cash flow.

web_blocks.title: Depreciation Lag Watch
paragraphs: FY2025 depreciation of property and equipment was $21,136M against $91,447M of CapEx, a 4.3x ratio [11]. Servers and network gear depreciate over 4–6 years, while data-center buildings run longer. As a result, the 2025–2026 CapEx wave ($195B–$205B guided for FY2026) will add tens of billions in annual depreciation to Cost of Revenues over 2027–2030 [7].

book_paragraphs: To understand how Alphabet turns a fraction of a cent on a search query into $164.7 billion of annual operating cash flow, you and I have to follow the plumbing from the moment a user types a query to the moment free cash flow lands in the treasury. On the front end, Alphabet's advertising business is a model of low-friction distribution. Millions of small businesses and global brands log into Google Ads, set a daily budget, and bid in automated auctions. There is no army of commissioned salespeople required to close a $500-a-month local plumber—the software does the selling.

The primary toll on that traffic is Traffic Acquisition Costs, or TAC. In FY2025, Alphabet paid out $59.9 billion in TAC—mostly revenue shares to browser and device partners like Apple to keep Google Search front-and-center, plus payouts to third-party website publishers in the Google Network. Here is the subtle structural tailwind: because high-margin Search and YouTube are growing much faster than the third-party Google Network, the overall TAC rate actually edged down from 20.7% of ad revenue in 2024 to 20.3% in 2025. Meanwhile, receivables turn over briskly on 30-day terms or instant card billing, meaning Alphabet doesn't tie up cash financing customer inventory.

On the back end, however, Alphabet runs one of the most capital-intensive physical supply chains in corporate history. Unlike pure software companies that rent someone else's cloud, Alphabet designs its own custom AI chips—Tensor Processing Units, or TPUs—fabricates them via partners like Broadcom and TSMC, and installs them inside company-owned hyperscale data centers wired together by private subsea fiber cables. Owning the TPU stack gives Alphabet a massive unit-cost edge when serving billions of AI Overviews and Gemini prompts, because it isn't paying Nvidia's gross margin on every internal inference call.

Look at the FY2025 waterfall to see how cleanly the P&L converts to cash—and where the tension lies. Out of $402.8 billion in revenue, Cost of Revenues (including that $59.9 billion TAC and data-center operating costs) took $162.5 billion, leaving a 59.7% gross margin. Research and development absorbed $61.1 billion—mostly elite engineering compensation—while Sales, Marketing, and G&A combined for $50.2 billion. That left $129.0 billion in operating income, a 32.0% operating margin. Add back $21.1 billion in non-cash depreciation, $25.0 billion in stock-based compensation, and favorable working capital, and operating cash flow reached an astonishing $164.7 billion.

But look at the final step of the waterfall: $91.4 billion went straight back out the door as Capital Expenditures for data centers, servers, and AI infrastructure, leaving $73.3 billion in free cash flow. And here is the watchpoint you cannot ignore: FY2025 depreciation was $21.1 billion, less than a quarter of FY2025 CapEx. When a company spends $91 billion in 2025 and guides to $195–$205 billion in 2026, those assets don't stay off the income statement forever. Over the next four to six years, depreciation will march steadily upward, meaning revenue growth—especially in Google Cloud and AI monetization—must keep pace just to hold operating margins flat.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The genius of Alphabet's unit economics is that Search and YouTube still print cash at >40% operating margins with negative-to-neutral working capital, funding the entire AI silicon buildout internally—until 2026, when $195B–$205B of CapEx temporarily outran even Alphabet's $165B+ operating cash flow.
